prompt: Where does the agent loop run when a program calls query() from the Claude Agent SDK?

choices.text: In a Claude Code subprocess the SDK starts
choices.why: Right. The SDK ships the CLI and exchanges JSON lines with it.

choices.text: On Anthropic's servers, as a hosted agent that the SDK calls over HTTPS
choices.why: The CLI calls the model provider; the loop itself runs on this machine.

choices.text: In a Python loop inside your own process, like lesson 8's Runner
choices.why: That is the OpenAI SDK's design, not this one.

choices.text: Inside labllm
choices.why: labllm is the model provider; it decides nothing about the loop.

prompt: The first run's result said cost_usd=0.1370. What is that number?

choices.text: The amount labllm charged the lab's key
choices.why: labllm charges nothing; the CLI computed the number.

choices.text: The CLI's own estimate, not a bill
choices.why: Right. It comes from the CLI's price table, guessed for a model it did not recognise; its size came from real token counts.

choices.text: The price of the subprocess's CPU time
choices.why: Compute time is not priced by the CLI.

choices.text: A fixed fee for each query() call, whatever it sends
choices.why: The later runs cost far less for the same answer.

prompt: What name did the model see for the get_order tool of the server called shop?

choices.text: shop.get_order
choices.why: The separator is a double underscore, and there is a prefix.

choices.text: get_order
choices.why: The server's name is part of it.

choices.text: mcp_shop_get_order_tool
choices.why: The separators are doubled, and nothing follows the tool's name.

choices.text: mcp__shop__get_order
choices.why: Right. mcp, the server's name and the tool's name, joined by double underscores.

prompt: Why does the get_order handler in cs_tools.py use json.dumps itself?

choices.text: MCP content is text the tool writes itself
choices.why: Right. A tool returns content blocks, so lesson 8's str() problem does not arise.

choices.text: Because the CLI rejects dictionaries larger than one kilobyte
choices.why: No such limit appears in the lesson.

choices.text: To encrypt the order before it crosses the pipe
choices.why: JSON is an encoding, not encryption.

choices.text: Because the model only reads JSON
choices.why: A model reads any text; JSON is chosen for clarity.

prompt: How many tools did the first request of the default run offer?
The run passed its own system_prompt and yet the request carried Bash, Edit and WebFetch. Why?

choices.text: Because the system prompt asked for them
choices.why: SYSTEM names no such tools.

choices.text: The tools option sets them, and it was left out
choices.why: Right. tools=[] removed them; system_prompt only replaced the prompt.

choices.text: Because allowed_tools listed them
choices.why: allowed_tools listed two shop tools and decides approval, not existence.

choices.text: Because labllm adds its own tools to every request
choices.why: labllm logs what arrived; it adds nothing.

prompt: Besides cost, why does the lesson say to start the tool list from nothing?

choices.text: Because the CLI refuses to start with more than ten tools offered
choices.why: It started with twenty-three.

choices.text: Because built-in tools stop the shop's tools from working
choices.why: The shop's tools worked in the default run.

choices.text: A support agent was handed a shell it never needed
choices.why: Right. Every offered tool is one the model is able to call; least privilege is lesson 17's subject.

choices.text: Speed
choices.why: Latency was nearly the same in both runs.

prompt: With no permission_mode, the refund run took over nine seconds. What was the CLI doing?

choices.text: Waiting for a person to type an answer
choices.why: No callback was set in that run.

choices.text: Running the refund and rolling it back
choices.why: The refund never ran.

choices.text: Retrying the agent's own request after a 404
choices.why: The 404 was for the classifier's model, not the agent's request.

choices.text: Asking a classifier, eleven times, whether the call was safe
choices.why: Right. Auto mode sent the conversation to a classifier model; no verdict came back.

prompt: The dontAsk refusal told the model it may reach the goal with other tools. Why did that not matter in cs_refund.py?

choices.text: Because the model was scripted to obey
choices.why: The script is the lab's; the boundary has to hold for a real model.

choices.text: tools=[] left no other tool to use
choices.why: Right. The refusal holds because of what the session contains.

choices.text: Because dontAsk also deletes the database's write permission
choices.why: Permission modes do not touch files.

choices.text: Because the message is not sent to the model
choices.why: It was sent; the log shows it as the tool result.

prompt: Why did can_use_tool never see the get_order calls?

choices.text: allowed_tools approved get_order first
choices.why: Right. The SDK's warning says so: an allowed entry shadows the callback.

choices.text: Because the model never called get_order in those runs
choices.why: The warning is about every get_order call, whatever the model did.

choices.text: Because callbacks only receive tools whose names start with refund
choices.why: Callbacks receive any call that reaches them.

choices.text: Because read-only tools skip the permission system
choices.why: No tool is marked read-only in cs_tools.py.

prompt: What can lesson 8's to_state() do that can_use_tool cannot?

choices.text: Show the person the call's arguments before anything runs
choices.why: can_use_tool receives them too; ask_a_person printed them.

choices.text: Deny with a message for the model
choices.why: PermissionResultDeny carries a message.

choices.text: Approve every future refund at once, from a single decision
choices.why: Neither approves future calls; each is decided separately.

choices.text: Wait for an answer given tomorrow, by another process
choices.why: Right. can_use_tool answers while the run waits, in the same process.

prompt: After the approved run, how many cents did the refunds table hold for M-1047?
In the hooked run, why was nobody asked about the refund of 7780 cents?

choices.text: Because allowed_tools contained the refund tool
choices.why: Only get_order was allowed.

choices.text: The PreToolUse hook denied it before the permission rules ran
choices.why: Right. The call never reached can_use_tool, so the n on standard input was never read.

choices.text: Because the order had already been refunded in full
choices.why: The hook refused on the amount, against LIMIT.

choices.text: The model cancelled the call
choices.why: The model asked; the hook answered.

prompt: Which of these did the hook in cs_refund.py do? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: Wrote an audit line for the refused refund
choices.why: Right. It writes before it decides.

choices.text: Wrote an audit line for the allowed get_order call
choices.why: Right. A hook sees allowed calls too.

choices.text: Asked a person before denying
choices.why: It denied in code, with no person.

choices.text: Changed the refund to 5000 cents and let it run
choices.why: It denied the call; it did not rewrite it.

prompt: With resume, why could the second message be answered?

choices.text: Because labllm remembered the earlier request
